Proposals for new public toilets, retail kiosks, beach chalets and a cafe in Filey have been revealed by North Yorkshire Council.
The planned redevelopment follows the closure of the existing cafe and toilet block at Royal Parade after structural issues were identified, according to the council.
A spokesperson said the plans were at an early stage but could represent an investment of up to £2.4m.
Council leader Carl Les said: "We know how important Royal Parade is and it's vital that our communities have access to high quality public facilities."
"We were left with little choice but to reluctantly close the toilets and café earlier this year for safety reasons, and we have always been clear that we wanted to explore opportunities to find a long-term solution for the site."
Further development work will be undertaken in the coming months, making use of feedback from councillors and the community, the authority said.
Its preferred scheme would result in new public conveniences, a replacement cafe, retail units and an increased number of beach chalets being made available.
Local councillors previously raised concerns about a lack of urgency and certainty to replace the scheme over the last 18 months.
Les said: "The site presents a number of challenges, but we are confident the plans that have been drawn up would provide upgraded, modern facilities that enhance the appeal of Filey as one of North Yorkshire's most popular coastal destinations.
"We look forward to seeing these plans develop in more detail through engagement with and by listening to local stakeholders."
Following further development work, the scheme will be considered by the council's executive members.

Summer heatwave put bin crews lives at risk, says council worker
ByAlec Doyle
Local Democracy Reporter
Published
Some bin collections were missed over the summer in a county partly because the heatwave became so serious it posed a risk to the lives of workers, a council worker has said.
Flintshire County Council's Chris Goddard said crews faced a "perfect storm" of challenges during the UK's record-breaking hot weather, causing a spate of widespread missed collections.
During the summer, drought was declared in all of Wales and wildfires caused devastation in parts of the country.
Goddard said: "We do have to make some difficult decisions but ultimately if there is a fatality in the workplace because of a decision I've made, that's something that I would have to live with – and probably defend."
Despite the missed collections the council remained on target to hit the Welsh government's national 70% waste recycling target this year, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.
Goddard, the council's streetscene service manager, said: "We had maybe five or six operational challenges that all came at the same time in a perfect storm this summer.
"Unfortunately, the heatwave was one of them and it was a contributing factor. We do have to prioritise staff safety above all else.
"My number one job every day is to make sure that everybody goes home safely and we take that really seriously within streetscene. That was only one of several contributing factors.
"That level of change is naturally going to cause a few bumps in the road, particularly with staff being asked to do a little bit more. There were some staffing issues during that period too."
Councillors praised Flintshire residents for largely embracing three-weekly residual waste collections and ensuring that the authority remained on-target to hit its statutory recycling rate.
"Three-weekly was very controversial at the time it came in," said Saltney councillor Richard Lloyd.
"It's quite clear to see now that the three-weekly black bin collection has been a good new factor. Recycling has improved at the kerbside."
Councillors said in the authority's meeting the change to three-weekly bin collections meant the council should still hit target despite the disruption.
The council also cut the amount of waste it sent to landfill or Parc Adfer by 6,467.49 tonnes between 2024 and 2026, and that improvement continued this year despite problems this summer.

Mr Toilet, a sim where you run a public restroom and charge for entry, is out now on Xbox Series X|S for $9.99.
Xbox players can charge strangers to use a toilet. You set the entry fee, keep the soap, toilet paper, and paper towels stocked, and throw out anyone who won’t pay. The store’s own tagline sums it up: “Your toilet – your rules. Clean, charge fees, kick out freeloaders.”
FreeMind S.A. developed and published the game, and FreeMind says it’s out now. The Xbox store listing says it costs $9.99 in the US store and has a release date of 11 November 2026.
The listing describes a single-player game optimised for Xbox Series X|S, which supports Xbox achievements and Xbox cloud saves. Your job is to make sure “everyone pays, nobody trashes the place, and no one smokes in the stalls.” Along the way you can invest in automation, special items, and decorations.
The ESRB rated it Everyone, with content descriptors for “Alcohol And Tobacco Reference, Crude Humor”, so expect the jokes to stay at toilet level.
Xbox is the game’s third platform. Mr Toilet is already on PS5 and Steam, where its demo took part in Steam Next Fest. Its Steam page shows a “Very Positive” user rating, with 89% of 88 reviews positive.

SENATOR Loren Legarda is calling for stronger protection for workers exposed to extreme heat, urging employers to adopt safer working hours and proposing additional compensation for those required to work under hazardous conditions.
The proposal is the third point of her 10-Point Policy Action Plan against El Niño, launched October 19, which focuses on protecting farmers, construction workers, fisherfolk, and others whose livelihoods require prolonged outdoor work.
“We cannot simply tell workers to avoid the heat. What about farmers who have to work in the fields? What about construction workers who need to earn a living to support their families? If we know that the heat has become dangerous, there must be clear measures to protect them without taking away their livelihoods,” Legarda said.
Under the proposal, physically demanding outdoor work should be moved to cooler hours, particularly when the heat index reaches 42 degrees Celsius. She is also proposing climate hazard pay for workers whose duties cannot be rescheduled, emphasizing that additional compensation must not replace workplace safety measures.
According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), a heat index of 42°C to 51°C falls under the danger category, when prolonged exposure increases the risk of heat cramps, exhaustion, and heatstroke. Temperatures of 52°C and above are classified as extreme danger.

The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), through Labor Advisory No. 20, Series of 2026, issued October 27, has urged employers to strengthen heat protection through risk assessments, adequate drinking water, cooling facilities, rest periods, and adjusted work arrangements.
Legarda stressed that these measures must reach high-risk workplaces, particularly farms and construction sites.
Advertisement
She also called for closer coordination among DOLE, local government units, employers, and workers' organizations to translate Pagasa warnings into timely workplace decisions. These include adjusting work-rest schedules, monitoring heat conditions, training workers to recognize heat-related illnesses, and preparing emergency response procedures.
The proposal aligns with Republic Act No. 11058, which strengthens occupational safety and health standards and requires employers to address workplace hazards.
Legarda emphasized that climate hazard pay would provide an additional layer of protection without replacing existing safety obligations. Under DOLE Labor Advisory No. 19, Series of 2026, workers covered by the Employees' Compensation Program may qualify for benefits for work-related heat stress and illnesses, subject to applicable requirements. These benefits are separate from the additional compensation she is proposing.
The initiative also relates to Legarda's Senate Bill No. 520, or the proposed Calamity Work Compensation Act, which seeks additional compensation for private-sector employees required to work during declared calamities and emergency alerts. While it does not automatically establish climate hazard pay for all periods of extreme heat, it recognizes the need to compensate workers facing extraordinary risks.
Advertisement
As principal author and sponsor of Republic Act No. 9729, or the Climate Change Act of 2009, and principal author of Republic Act No. 10692, or the Pagasa Modernization Act of 2015, Legarda has advanced measures supporting climate adaptation and early warning systems.
She also filed Senate Resolution No. 733 seeking an inquiry into government preparedness for the anticipated strong to very strong El Niño and its potential effects on water supply, food production, livelihoods, and vulnerable communities.
With El Niño potentially persisting into the first quarter of 2027 and its effects extending through the first half of the year, Legarda stressed the urgency of protecting workers.
“Workers should not have to choose between their health and their families’ income. Both are equally important. We already know the dangers of extreme heat, so preparedness must come first,” she said.

She urged government agencies and employers to enforce existing safety requirements and examine additional measures to ensure workers remain protected while sustaining their livelihoods.

Red alert: Bay of Bengal low-pressure area expected to intensify into cyclonic storm
November 13, 2026 at
5:58 PM
Naval and fishing communities have been strictly warned not to venture into deep-sea areas off Sri Lanka’s coasts and the southeastern Bay of Bengal starting at 5:30AM tomorrow (Nov.14), as a low-pressure system is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm.
The Department of Meteorology’s Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre issued a red “TAKE ACTION” bulletin at 5PM on November 13 , valid until November 15 .The system, currently located over the southeastern Bay of Bengal, is projected to move northwestwards and strengthen into a depression by November 15, before further developing into a cyclonic storm over the central Bay of Bengal around November 16.
The restriction applies to deep-sea areas bounded by 05N-15N and 80E-90E, as well as coastal waters extending from Kankasanthurai to Hambantota via Trincomalee and Pottuvil. Individuals currently operating within these dangerous zones are strongly advised to relocate to safe areas immediately and remain alert to upcoming bulletins. (Newswire)

Yellow alert for thunderstorms and rain in Rajasthan:Weather to change in parts of Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner and Phalodi
Winter conditions in Rajasthan are expected to intensify from the beginning of next week. An active western disturbance over North India is likely to bring light rain to parts of the state's north-western region on 14 November, bringing a change in weather conditions.
The Meteorological Department has forecast cloudy skies and light rain at isolated places in five districts of the Jodhpur and Bikaner divisions on 14 November due to the western disturbance.
From 16 November, after the western disturbance moves away, cold northerly winds are expected to begin blowing across Rajasthan. This will lead to a rise in night-time chill in several cities across the state.
Looking at the weather over the past 24 hours, skies remained clear and there was mild sunshine across most parts of the state, except the northern region. In the Sri Ganganagar area, light clouds and haze appeared in the sky on Thursday afternoon. Light winds accompanied the cloud cover, making the weather cooler by evening. Light clouds also appeared over some parts of Hanumangarh late in the evening.
Daytime maximum temperatures crossed 35°C in Barmer, Chittorgarh and Churu. The temperature was recorded at 36.3°C in Barmer, 36°C in Chittorgarh and 35.2°C in Churu. Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Pilani recorded 34.7°C, while Nagaur recorded 33.7°C.
Weak northerly winds causing temperature fluctuations
According to weather experts, a western disturbance is active over parts of North India, including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Punjab and Haryana. The system has brought cloud cover to these areas and weakened northerly winds. As a result, temperatures are fluctuating across parts of Rajasthan.
On Thursday, maximum temperatures fell by up to 2 degrees in Phalodi, Barmer, Jaisalmer, Pratapgarh, Sirohi and Dungarpur. Meanwhile, maximum temperatures rose by up to 2 degrees in Ajmer, Alwar, Churu, Jaipur, Pilani, Sikar and Sri Ganganagar.
Mount Abu records the coldest night
Along with maximum temperatures, minimum temperatures also fluctuated on Thursday. Mount Abu recorded the coldest night, with the minimum temperature at 11.6°C. The minimum temperature was 12°C in Sikar, 12.4°C in Bhilwara, 14.3°C in Ajmer, 14.5°C in Alwar, 14.9°C in Churu, 14.4°C in Chittorgarh and 14.2°C in Udaipur.
The system may also have a mild impact on these areas, as well as the Shekhawati region, on 15 November. From 16 November, temperatures in most cities across the state are expected to fall by 2 to 3 degrees.
Weather conditions in major Rajasthan cities
In Jaipur, the sky remained clear throughout Thursday, with pleasant sunshine. Sunshine continued from morning until late evening, and the maximum temperature was recorded at 32.6°C. As evening set in, light cool winds began blowing across the city and continued until late at night. Jaipur recorded a minimum temperature of 17.1°C.
The sky remained clear throughout the day in Jaipur on Thursday, with sunshine continuing until late evening.
Sikar remained warm throughout Thursday. After light clouds appeared last night, bright sunshine prevailed during the day. The weather in Sikar remains dry. At the Fatehpur weather station in Sikar, the maximum temperature was recorded at 34°C and the minimum at 11.9°C. No significant change in temperatures is expected in Sikar for now.
Sikar witnessed bright sunshine throughout the day on Thursday. The weather remained dry.
Temperatures continue to fluctuate in Udaipur. The maximum temperature was recorded at 32.4°C and the minimum at 14.4°C. On 10 November, the maximum temperature had been 34°C and the minimum 14.6°C.
This means that over the two days, the daytime temperature fell by 1.6 degrees and the night-time temperature by 0.2 degrees. The heat is still being felt during the day, while mornings and nights are becoming cooler.
Udaipur continued to experience fluctuations in temperature, with the effects of heat still being felt.
Daytime temperatures in Kota are still rising. While the temperature was 31.3°C on Wednesday, it increased to 32.4°C on Thursday. The minimum temperature, however, fell from 17.1°C to 15.7°C.
Daytime temperatures in Kota are continuing to rise, while night-time temperatures are falling.
Temperatures have fallen in Jodhpur. The maximum temperature on Thursday was recorded at 34.7°C, which was 3 degrees above normal. The minimum temperature was 17.5°C, 2 degrees above normal. On Wednesday, the maximum and minimum temperatures were 35.2°C and 18.3°C, respectively.
The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 14 and 15 November this week. Rain accompanied by lightning is likely on 14 November. Cloudy skies and rain are also expected on 15 November.
Ajmer recorded a maximum temperature of 33.5°C and a minimum of 14.3°C on Thursday. The difference between the daytime and night-time temperatures was 19.2 degrees. A fall in night-time temperatures has brought a slight chill during the morning and late-night hours.
Ajmer recorded a maximum temperature of 33.5 degrees Celsius on Thursday.
The weather remained normal in Alwar on Thursday. Sunshine during the day pushed the maximum temperature to 31.6°C. However, cooler conditions continued in the morning and evening. Temperatures are gradually falling at night, bringing increased chill.
As a result, the difference between daytime and night-time weather has become more noticeable. The Meteorological Department has forecast a rise in temperatures over the coming days. This may increase the heat during the day, while mild cool conditions are likely to persist in the mornings and evenings.
The weather remained normal in Alwar on Thursday, with bright sunshine during the day.

Johannesburg residents have been urged to take precautions as extremely hot temperatures are expected to persist across most parts of the city on Friday. The City of Johannesburg’s Emergency Management Services (EMS) has advised residents to stay hydrated, drink plenty of water and avoid direct exposure to sunlight, particularly between 11am and 3pm.
EMS spokesperson Robert Mulaudzi said people working outdoors should take regular breaks to protect themselves against heat-related illnesses. “Residents are encouraged to continue to stay hydrated, drink lots of water and avoid direct sunlight, especially between 11am and 3pm,” Mulaudzi said.
He added that people working directly in the sun should take regular breaks.Meanwhile, the South African Weather Service’s early forecast indicates a 60% chance of rainfall on Saturday, increasing to 80% on Sunday.
Mulaudzi urged residents to remain cautious and prepare for possible weather-related emergencies. “The City of Joburg EMS will be monitoring all seven regions of the city for any emergencies which might occur,” he said.
